starter.heading: Do now
items: Name the three states of matter.
Which state has particles furthest apart?
starter.notes: Retrieval from last lesson; take answers cold.

entries.definition: A very small piece of a substance, too small to see.
Particles packed closely and only vibrating.
Particles touching but able to move past each other.
Particles far apart and moving freely.

vocabulary.notes: Say each term aloud and have the class repeat it.

content.heading: The particle model
content.body: Everything is made of tiny particles. How they are arranged and how they move decides whether a substance is a solid, a liquid or a gas.
content.notes: Draw the three particle diagrams on the board.

worked-example.heading: Worked example
worked-example.question: Why does an ice cube left on a plate turn into a puddle?
steps: Room air is warmer than the ice, so energy passes into it.
They break free and slide past each other: the ice melts.
worked-example.notes: Reveal one step at a time.

true-false.statement: Particles in a solid do not move at all.
true-false.notes: Ask for hands up before revealing.

multiple-choice.stem: In which state of matter are the particles furthest apart?

options.text: They are the same in all three

multiple-choice.explanation: Gas particles move freely with large gaps between them.
multiple-choice.notes: Watch for the misconception that liquids are the most spread out.

sort.stem: Put these in order of increasing particle energy.
sort.notes: Pupils order the cards in pairs.

items: Describe the particles in a liquid.
Name the change of state from gas to liquid.
Predict what happens to a gas when it is cooled.
exit-ticket.footnote: Answer on a sticky note and hand it in.
exit-ticket.notes: Collect and sort into three piles.

discussion.prompt: Why does a wet playground dry faster on a windy day?

matching.stem: Match each state to its particles.

fill-gap.sentence: Ice ___ when it is heated and water ___ when it is cooled.

open-response.stem: Explain why a balloon shrinks in a fridge.
open-response.modelAnswer: The gas particles lose energy, move less and take up less room.

items: We can describe particles in each state
We can name the changes of state
